candidate.answerReason: The apex angles of the two isosceles triangles are the acute angles of right triangle ABE, so they sum to 90°. Their corresponding base angles at C and D consequently sum to 135°.

methods.label: Combine the two isosceles angle sums
methods.explanation:
The perpendicular intersection connects the apex angles of the two isosceles triangles. We can use their sum without finding either angle separately.

Let \(x=\angle BAC\) and \(y=\angle ABD\). Since \(E\) lies on segments \(AC\) and \(BD\), these are also \(\angle BAE\) and \(\angle ABE\). Triangle \(ABE\) is right at \(E\), so
\[
x+y=90^\circ.
\]
In triangle \(ABC\), the equality \(AB=AC\) makes the angles at \(B\) and \(C\) equal. The triangle angle sum therefore gives
\[
\angle C=\frac{180^\circ-x}{2}.
\]
Likewise, \(AB=BD\) makes the angles at \(A\) and \(D\) in triangle \(ABD\) equal, with apex angle \(y\) at \(B\). Thus
\[
\angle D=\frac{180^\circ-y}{2}.
\]
Adding eliminates the individual unknown angles:
\[
\angle C+\angle D
=\frac{360^\circ-(x+y)}{2}
=\frac{360^\circ-90^\circ}{2}
=\boxed{135^\circ}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
